speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history. Given the chronic nature of your symptoms and your history of diabetes, I need to rule out cervical radiculopathy or a cervical myelopathy. Have you noticed any numbness in your legs, difficulty with balance, or changes in bowel or bladder function?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Superimposed Diabetic Neuropathy.

The combination of progressive bilateral hand weakness, burning pain, and paresthesias in a 58-year-old male with a chronic cervical spine issue strongly suggests spinal cord compression (myelopathy) rather than simple radiculopathy, although his diabetes may contribute to peripheral neuropathy symptoms. The MRI results are crucial to confirm spinal cord signal changes or compression.
